kjv: Praise ye the LORD for the avenging of Israel
mine: When the leaders took the lead in Israel
note: Bifroa' pera'ot is obscure: the root para' means "let loose (hair)", and pera'ot likely means "leaders" (cf. Deut 32:42) or "when locks hung loose" (warriors' vow); "avenging" follows a guess with no firm basis in the Hebrew. Context: when the leaders took the lead (medium confidence). Para' means 'let loose (hair)'; pera'ot is either 'leaders' (cf. Arabic far' 'top, chief'; LXX(A) 'when leaders led'; 5:9 'the commanders of Israel') or 'loose locks' of warriors under a vow (cf. Deut 32:42). The parallel 'people offered themselves' suits either. ESV, NIV, NASB and CSB read 'leaders'; NRSV and NJPS 'locks'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'when locks hang loose/long in Israel', a war vow — NRSV, NJPS, many commentators (cf. Num 6:5); (2) 'for the avenging of Israel', from Aramaic pur'anuta 'retribution' — Targum, Rashi, KJV; (3) 'when a revelation was revealed' — LXX(B).

mine: The mountains quaked before Yahweh, the One of Sinai
note: Nazelu may be from nazal "flow" (KJV) or zalal "quake" (LXX, cf. Isa 64:1); zeh sinay is an old divine title "the One of Sinai" (cf. Ps 68:8), not a demonstrative pointing at the mountain. Context: quaked (medium confidence). MT points nazelu 'flowed' (nazal), but the same consonants read nazollu 'quaked' (zalal), as LXX esaleuthesan and Isa 63:19 [64:1]; 5:4 describes earthquake and storm. ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV and NJPS all read 'quaked'. 'Flowed/melted' with MT's vowels (cf. Mic 1:4; Ps 97:5) stays possible. Zeh sinay is a divine title (cf. Ps 68:9). Other possible meanings: (1) 'the mountains flowed/melted' — MT vocalization, Targum, KJV; (2) 'even this Sinai' or 'that Sinai', a demonstrative pointing to the mountain — KJV, ESV, NASB, rather than the title 'the One of Sinai' (NIV, NRSV, NJPS).

mine: you who sit on rich carpets
note: Middin is plural of mad "cloth, carpet" (the KJV took it from din "judge"); the line contrasts riders, the seated wealthy, and walkers.

kjv: [They that are delivered] from the noise of archers
mine: To the sound of the musicians
note: Mechatsetsim is uncertain (archers, those dividing flocks, or singers); the KJV supplies a subject not in the Hebrew.

kjv: Then he made him that remaineth have dominion over the nobles
mine: Then the survivors came down to the nobles
note: The MT points yerad as from radah "rule", which the KJV follows; the parallel yerad-li and the context of descending to battle favour "came down" (yarad), as in LXX.

kjv: a root of them against Amalek ... the pen of the writer
mine: those whose root is in Amalek ... the marshal's staff
note: Shoresham ba'amaleq means their roots are in (the hill country of) Amalek (cf. 12:15); shevet sofer is the staff of the muster officer, not a writing pen.
Miftsarim (only here) are inlets or harbours on the coast; "breaches" is an etymological guess from parats "break".

kjv: O my soul, thou hast trodden down strength
mine: March on, my soul, with strength
note: Tidreki is imperfect/jussive, a self-exhortation; 'oz is adverbial "with might", not the object trodden.

kjv: Then were the horsehoofs broken by the means of the pransings
mine: Then the horses' hooves hammered with the galloping
note: Halemu means "struck, pounded" (the drumming of hooves); nothing is broken. Dahar is galloping.
Chem'ah is curdled milk or yogurt, a refreshing drink, not butter in the modern sense.
Machaqah (hapax) means crush or shatter; the parallel with the tent peg through the temple (4:21) shows no beheading.
